speaker: Doctor
text: I am ready to help. Please describe your wrist pain and any difficulty you are experiencing with hand movement, including when it started and what makes it better or worse.

speaker: Patient
text: 34-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing pain in her right thumb and wrist, which radiates to her elbow for the past three months. The pain worsens when she holds her infant son and is alleviated somewhat with an ice pack. She mentions a history of falling on her right outstretched hand about six months ago. She also notes that her mother has a history of chronic joint pain treated with methotrexate. The patient has been taking ibuprofen as needed for her symptoms.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: De Quervain's Tenosynovitis. The history of a fall six months ago likely caused the initial injury, leading to chronic inflammation of the abductor pollicis longus and extensor pollicis brevis tendons, exacerbated by repetitive lifting of an infant. The pain radiating to the elbow and relief with ice are consistent with this overuse injury.
